title: A fixed-rate tail test overstates the conflict between two sparse dust-onset surveys
abstract: We audit the claimed conflict between two field-dwarf dust-onset surveys. The earlier rate uses one event. That event, G2870, also appears in the later survey. We reproduce the published fixed-rate tail probability near 1e-8 for nine later events. Under a common Poisson event population and the headline fixed exposures, a conditional test that counts shared events once gives a conservative one-sided probability of 0.05144 for two confirmed events, or 0.21153 if seven unclear events are dust. An independent-count calculation would give 0.07428 but does not apply to the shared event. We derive a bound over unknown shared exposure and check its size by exact enumeration. We also show that the reported two-sided 95 percent rate range uses central 90 percent quantiles; its one-sided upper bound remains valid. Different event templates and star cuts prevent a direct physical rate comparison. Deeper templates give conditional probabilities near 0.023, so we do not establish agreement. The fixed-rate tail does not establish a conflict between measured rates. This is an audit of published aggregate results, not new photometry. Code, source hashes, results, and a figure are included.
